problem: Pretrained end-to-end visual navigation policies (e.g. DD-PPO) that reach near-perfect success on clean scenes collapse under simple visual corruptions such as dim lighting, rain or noise. Existing test-time adaptation methods either need gradient updates and batches, or are not designed for real-time navigation.
motivation: Robots need to keep navigating when sensory input shifts abruptly, and adaptation must be instantaneous and lightweight. Biological perception, framed by the Free Energy Principle as prediction-error plus Bayesian-surprise minimisation, suggests combining top-down reconstruction with feature-distribution re-normalisation.
key_idea: Adapt BatchNorm statistics per frame (Adaptive Normalisation) and feed the policy a clean surrogate observation reconstructed by a frozen Top-down Decoder from the adapted features, with no gradient updates at test time.
insight: Ablation: AN-Only (avg SR 0.89) far outperforms TD-Only (0.75), so normalisation is the main source of robustness, while TD+AN across all blocks gives the best average and minimum (0.92 SR / 0.83 min SR), so the decoder adds complementary value. Adapting only a single block with TD is worse (0.84), so adaptation must be applied hierarchically. An empirical kNN KL estimate shows AN pulls corrupted features toward clean ones in 7 of 8 corruptions, which supports the Bayesian-surprise interpretation. Instance statistics (rho=1) work better than running averages for abrupt shifts.
method: Pretrained-Nav: DD-PPO point-goal policy with GroupNorm replaced by BatchNorm and fine-tuned 120M frames; SE-ResNeXt-50 visual encoder + 512-d LSTM policy.
Top-down Decoder (TD): 5.3M-parameter residual decoder reconstructing 256x256 RGB from VE block-3 features, trained with MSE on 112k clean Gibson frames with frozen VE.

Adaptive Normalisation (AN): BatchNorm statistics updated every step by moving average (Running, adaptive rho) or by instance statistics only (Instance, rho=1), so no batch is needed and no gradients are used.
Surrogate re-encoding: the TD output is re-encoded by the VE with the original training statistics and passed to the LSTM policy.

Theory: VFE decomposed into prediction error (reconstruction proxy) and Bayesian surprise (moment-matching proxy); a proposition under mean-field, Gaussian and spatial-ergodicity assumptions shows normalisation reduces KL to the prior.

Real-robot pipeline: VE initialised from the Habitat model, policy trained by behavioural cloning (L1) on ~300 episodes/3h with a Tello drone, TD also trained on real images, computation on a ground station.

setting.backbone: SE-ResNeXt-50 visual encoder + LSTM policy (DD-PPO, BatchNorm variant, frozen at test time) + 5.3M residual Top-down Decoder
setting.training_data: DD-PPO policy pre-trained on ~2.5B Gibson frames + 120M frames fine-tune; decoder on 112k clean Gibson frames (72 training scenes); real-world: ~300 drone episodes (~3h) in one room for the policy
setting.action_space: Simulation: discrete forward 0.25 m / turn 10° / stop; real drone: continuous (dx,dy,dz,dyaw) waypoint-like actions (z omitted)

results: On Habitat Gibson point-goal navigation with 8 corruptions, FEP-Nav Instance reaches average SR 0.92 / SPL 0.79 and worst-case SR 0.83, beating the strongest baseline DUA (0.89 / 0.73, min 0.76) and Pretrained-Nav (0.73 / 0.53). On the real drone, average SR is 0.72 versus 0.54 for DUA and 0.40 for the vanilla policy.
limitations: Weaker under strong blur (defocus/motion), where DUA is better and MPRNet restoration is better, as high-frequency details cannot be recovered.
The theory relies on Gaussian, mean-field and ergodicity approximations, and it is only an FEP-inspired interpretation rather than exact VFE minimisation.
Adds an encode-decode pass (0.045 s per frame on a Jetson AGX Orin), and the real-world experiments are limited to a single room and one obstacle task with compute at a ground station.
